title: What are the four access modifiers in Java and their exact visibility?
shortTitle: What are the four access modifiers in Java?
keyPoints: public: visible everywhere, to any class in any package
protected: visible in the same package + subclasses in other packages
default (no keyword): visible only within the same package (package-private)
private: visible only within the same class (not even subclasses)
Top-level classes can only be public or package-private – not private or protected
In banking: fields are private, service methods are public, internal helpers are package-private

s1_definition.oneliner: Java has four access levels: public (everywhere), protected (same package + subclasses), default/package-private (same package), and private (same class only).
s1_definition.profdef:
Four levels from most open to most restricted:

- **public** – accessible from any class in any package. Use for API methods and service interfaces.
- **protected** – accessible within the same package, and by subclasses in other packages. Use sparingly for inheritance.
- **default (package-private)** – no keyword written. Accessible only within the same package. Use for internal implementation classes.
- **private** – accessible only within the declaring class. Not visible to subclasses or other classes. Use for all fields and internal methods.
s1_definition.analogy: A bank building with four security levels. Public areas (lobby) are open to everyone. Protected areas (back office) are accessible to employees of this branch and managers from other branches (subclasses). Package-private areas (operations room) are only for employees of this specific branch. Private areas (the vault) are accessible only to the vault officer (the class itself).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Access modifier visibility:

                Same class  Same package  Subclass (other pkg)  Other package
  public          Yes          Yes              Yes                  Yes
  protected       Yes          Yes              Yes                  No
  default         Yes          Yes              No                   No
  private         Yes          No               No                   No

  Top-level class: only public or default
  Inner class: all four modifiers allowed

  Banking pattern:
    Fields     → private (always)
    Getters    → public
    Behavior   → public (debit, credit)
    Helpers    → private or default
    Interfaces → public
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Java has four access modifiers that control visibility: public (everywhere), protected (same package plus subclasses), default or package-private (same package only, no keyword written), and private (same class only).

In banking code, the pattern is consistent. All fields are private to prevent external code from corrupting state. Public methods like debit() and credit() validate inputs and enforce business rules. Internal helper methods are private. Classes shared within the package but not with external code use package-private access.

Top-level classes can only be public or package-private. Private and protected are only for members inside a class. And since Java 9, the module system adds another layer: even public classes must be explicitly exported from their module to be visible to other modules.

One sentence to remember: public means everywhere, protected means package plus subclasses, default means same package, private means same class – and fields should always be private.
